formula_differentiation.prompt: Both Gui Zhi Fu Ling Wan (Cinnamon Twig and Poria Pill) and Tao He Cheng Qi Tang (Peach Pit Decoction to Order the Qi) treat excess patterns with blood stasis in the lower abdomen with an etiology that involves both cold and heat, typically with cold pathogenic Qi leading to blood stasis in the Lower Jiao. This prevents the Yang Qi from connecting with the blood, so that it moves upward instead to cause symptoms like flushing or restlessness. What is their difference?

options.label: A
options.text: Tao He Cheng Qi Tang (Peach Pit Decoction to Order the Qi) treats patterns that are relatively more Yang or hot in nature that tend toward dryness, with symptoms that, as a result, are both more changeable and more severe such as flushed face, nosebleeds, mania, or more indistinct and moveable boundaries of tenderness on palpation of the abdomen. The pulse will be submerged, full, or choppy, the tongue coating may be yellow, and the patient may be thirsty.

options.label: B
options.text: Gui Zhi Fu Ling Wan (Cinnamon Twig and Poria Pill) patterns, on the other hand, also involve the accumulation of water and are thus more Yin in nature. This is reflected in a more stable symptomatology and fixed areas of tenderness on palpation. The pulse will be deep, slow, and tight, any tongue coating will usually be white, and the patient will generally not be thirsty, even if there are other heat signs.

options.label: C
options.text: Both of them

options.label: D
options.text: Neither are correct

classification.reason: Formula indication, pattern recognition or selection

es.prompt: Tanto Gui Zhi Fu Ling Wan (Cinnamon Twig and Poria Pill) como Tao He Cheng Qi Tang (Peach Pit Decoction to Order the Qi) tratan patrones de exceso con estasis de Sangre en el abdomen inferior con una etiología que implica tanto frío como calor, típicamente con Qi patógeno frío que conduce a estasis de Sangre en el Jiao Inferior. Esto impide que el Yang Qi se conecte con la sangre, de manera que se mueve hacia arriba en lugar de causar síntomas como la rotura o la inquilina. ¿En qué se diferencian?

options.label: A
options.text: Tao He Cheng Qi Tang (Peach Pit Decoction to Order the Qi) trata patrones que son relativamente más Yang o caliente en la naturaleza que tienden hacia la sequedad, con síntomas que, como resultado, son tanto más cambiantes y más severos como rostro enrojecido, hemorragias nasales, manía, o más límites indistintos y móviles de ternura en la palpación del abdomen. El pulso será sumergido, lleno o áspero, el saburra lingual puede ser amarillo, y el paciente puede tener sed.

options.label: B

IDENTIFICATION OF THE FORMULA ACCORDING TO THE GENERAL DESCRIPTION

Pattern: Spleen and Stomach Qi deficiency leading to sinking of the yang.

Action: Tonifies the Middle Burner, augments the Qi, raises the Yang, and lifts what has sunken.

Indications: This formula is used to treat three different patterns that may occur alone or in conjuntion with each other.

1) Spleen and Stomach deficiency with inability to raise the clear characterized by dizziness, unsteadiness, impaired or unclear vision, deafness, tinnitus, shortness of breath, laconic speech, a weak voice, a shiny, pale complexion, reduce intake of food, loose stools, a pale tongue, and a frail pulse.

2) Qi deficiency fever manifests as intermittent fever (that worsens upon exertion), spontaneous sweating, aversion to cold, a thirst for warm beverages, a pale tongue, and a large but forceless pulse.

3) Sinking in the Middle Burner Qi characterized by hemorrhoids, rectal or uterine prolapse, prolapse of the internal organs, chronic diarrhea or dysentery, irregular uterine bleeding, reduce intake of food, loose stools, a pale tongue, and a deficient and soft pulse.

The “flagship formula” of the “Tonify Earth” school. Originally indicated for Qi deficiency fevers and now widely used for conditions involving prolapse. May be modified to suit a variety of Qi deficiency presentations, including those with concurrent Liver depression Qi stagnation. This formula is contraindicated for fever due to Heat from Yin deficiency. This formula is not indicated in all instances of prolapse, but only in those due to Qi deficiency.

¿Qué fórmula corresponde a la descripción general a continuación?

Patrón: La deficiencia de bazo y Stomach Qi conduce al hundimiento del yang.

Acción: Tonifica el quemador medio, aumenta el Qi, levanta el Yang, y levanta lo que ha hundido.

Indicaciones: Esta fórmula se utiliza para tratar tres patrones diferentes que pueden ocurrir solos o en conjunción entre sí.

1) deficiencia de bazo y estómago con incapacidad para elevar lo claro caracterizado por mareo, inestable, visión deteriorada o poco clara, sordera, tinnitus, falta de aliento, habla laconica, voz débil, una tez brillante y pálida, reduce la ingesta de alimentos, heces sueltas, una lengua pálida y un pulso frágil.

2) La fiebre por deficiencia de Qi se manifiesta como fiebre intermitente (que empeora sobre el esfuerzo), sudor espontáneo, aversión al frío, una sed de bebidas calientes, una lengua pálida y un pulso grande pero sin fuerza.

3) Cantar en el Qi del quemador medio caracterizado por hemorroides, prolapso rectal o uterino, prolapso de los órganos internos, diarrea crónica o disentería, sangrado uterino irregular, reducir la ingesta de alimentos, heces sueltas, una lengua pálida y un pulso deficiente y suave.

La “fórmula ardiente” de la escuela “Tonificar la Tierra”. Originalmente indicado para fiebres por deficiencia de Qi y ahora ampliamente utilizado para condiciones que implican prolapso. Puede ser modificado para adaptarse a una variedad de presentaciones de deficiencia de Qi, incluyendo las concurrentes depresión del hígado Qi estancamiento. Esta fórmula está contraindicada para fiebre debido a calor por deficiencia de Yin. Esta fórmula no se indica en todos los casos de prolapso, sino sólo en aquellos debido a la deficiencia de Qi.

1-Pueraria-Scutellaria-Coptis Decoction (ge gen (Puerariae Radix) qin lian tang) / Kudzu, Scutellaria, and Coptis Decoction (ge gen huang qin huang lian tang (Kudzu, Scutellaria, and Coptis Decoction))

This formula treats dysenteric disorders due to damp-heat in the Yang Brightness Qi aspect. In this pattern, the exterior has not been completely relased, but the interior is already ablaze with heat. This can be caused by improper treatment of an exterior disorder with purgatives. A pathogen in the interior may or not present. Heat is more severe than dampness. This formula is appropiate where the prolapse occurs as a result of heat excess diarrhea.

Chief: Ge gen (Rx Puerariae)

Deputy: Huang lian (Rz Coptidis)

Assistant: Huang qin (Rx Scutellariae)

Envoy: Zhi gan cao (Rx Glycyrrhizae preparata)

2-Pulsatilla Decoction (bai tou weng tang (Pulsatilla Decoction))

Chief: Bai tou weng (Rx Pulsatillae) clears damp-heat and relieves fire toxin, especially in the blood level.

Deputy: Huang lian (Rz Coptidis) clears damp-heat from stomach and intestine and Huang bai (Cx Phellodendri) clears damp-heat from the lower burner.

Assistant: Qin pi (Cx Fraxini) drains dampness, resolves toxicity, and stops diarrhea.

3-Peony Decoction (shao yao tang (Peony Decoction))

The primary emphasis of this formula is to clear heat, dry dampness, and regulate Qi and Blood in order to guide out the cause of the disorder.

Chief: Huang lian (Rz Coptidis) and Huang qing (Rx Scutellariae), which resolve heat toxicity in the intestines by clearing heat and drying dampness.

Deputy: Da huang (Rhei Radix et Rhizoma), serves as the deputy to drain heat toxins through the stool. Shao yao (Rx Paeoniae), used in large dose to move the blood, expel the pus, relax urgency, and stop the pain. Dang gui (Rx Angelica sinensis), tonifies, warms, and moves the blood. Together, they regulate the nutritive Qi and Blood. When combined with Gan cao (Rx Glycyrrhizae), Shao yao (Rx Paeoniae) also moderates spasms and relieves abdominal pain.

Assistant: Rou gui (Cx Cinnamomi), this herbs enters the blood level and assists the blood-harmonizing herbs in moving the blood. It also acts as an opposing assistant, which means that it prevents the cold, bitter properties of the other herbs from either injuring the Yang or constraining the pathogenic influences in the interior and thereby transforming into smoldering damp-heat. The other assistants, Mu xiang (Rx Aucklandiae) and Bing lang (Sm Arecae), promote the movement of Qi and help eliminate stagnation.
